item.title: GitHub Actions cPanel CVE-2026-41940 Abuse, Iran OT Attacks, Ubuntu CVE-2026-8933
item.content:encoded:
Large-Scale GitHub Actions Abuse Powers a Distributed cPanel and WHM Exploitation Campaign — Must Read

A large campaign abused compromised GitHub repositories and GitHub Actions runners to download a Linux payload that scans for and exploits CVE-2026-41940 in cPanel and WHM, then steals server credentials and secrets. The malicious Packagist development versions were mainly evidence of the repository compromise, not the primary execution path.

  • A campaign abused compromised GitHub repositories by adding malicious GitHub Actions workflow files that launched GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners to download and run a Linux scanning and exploitation payload from 43[.]228[.]157[.]68.
  • The payload targeted internet-facing cPanel and WHM systems, attempted exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, and searched compromised servers for credentials, configuration files, environment variables, database access, SSH material, Git tokens, cloud keys, and payment service credentials.
  • Packagist synchronized malicious development versions across ten packages associated with the compromised developer dinushchathurya, but ordinary installation of those PHP packages did not automatically execute the malicious workflows.
  • GitHub Code Search found approximately 6,100 workflow files matching the campaign’s unique DNSHook identifier, while broader searches using related indicators returned roughly 15,000 to 16,000 matching files.
  • The workflows continuously reported execution status through a heartbeat endpoint and uploaded newly collected results through HTTP POST requests to threat actor-controlled infrastructure.

Federal agencies broaden alert on Iran-linked OT attacks — Must Read

Federal agencies expanded their warning about Iran-linked hackers targeting internet-exposed industrial control systems, now including Schneider Electric and Siemens PLCs in addition to Rockwell/Allen-Bradley. CISA, the FBI and EPA urged OT operators to restrict direct internet access and secure PLC deployments as attacks have already caused disruption and financial losses.

  • The federal government expanded an April warning about attacks on internet-facing operational technology by hackers affiliated with the Iranian regime.
  • The revised advisory broadened the manufacturer scope from Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley PLCs to include observed targeting of Schneider Electric, Siemens, and possible other PLC manufacturers.
  • Observed incidents included malicious project file interactions and manipulation of data on human machine interface and supervisory control and data acquisition displays.
  • Targeted organizations suffered operational disruption and financial loss, according to the advisory.
  • CISA, the FBI, and the EPA said pressure from Iran-affiliated attackers is expected to continue and urged OT owners and operators to restrict direct internet access and ensure secure PLC deployment.

Ubuntu snap-confine Flaw Could Give Local Users Root on Default Desktop Installs — Should Read

A high-severity snap-confine flaw, CVE-2026-8933, can let a local unprivileged user gain root access on default Ubuntu Desktop installs. Organizations should urgently apply the latest snapd updates and verify installed versions.

  • Cybersecurity researchers disclosed CVE-2026-8933, a high-severity local privilege escalation vulnerability in snap-confine that can allow an unprivileged user to obtain root access.
  • The flaw affects default installations of Ubuntu Desktop 24.04, 25.10, and 26.04.
  • Qualys said the issue stems from a security hardening change that introduced a race condition during sandbox initialization.
  • The exploit involves concurrent race conditions using a malicious FUSE file system and a symbolic link to redirect file operations to sensitive system locations.
  • Organizations are advised to apply the latest snapd updates and verify the installed snapd version.

South Korea discloses data breach impacting diplomats worldwide — Should Read

South Korea says hackers had access to the National Diplomatic Academy’s online education system for about ten months, stealing personal data for at least 6,000 current and former Foreign Ministry personnel, including diplomats abroad. The ministry says passwords were encrypted and no highly sensitive identifiers were exposed, but affected users are being warned to watch for suspicious emails.

  • South Korea disclosed that hackers breached the National Diplomatic Academy's online education system and stole personal information belonging to current and former Ministry of Foreign Affairs employees, including overseas diplomats.
  • The breach began in April 2025 after an unknown threat actor exploited a vulnerability in the Academy's server, and data was leaked between April 2025 and February 2026.
  • The incident impacts at least 6,000 individuals, including 350 current government attachés dispatched abroad.
  • The leaked data is estimated to include IDs, names, email addresses, and encrypted passwords, while the ministry said unique identification numbers, sensitive information, mobile phone numbers, photographs, and home addresses were not exposed.
  • The Ministry of Foreign Affairs blocked access to the online education system, implemented additional security measures, and advised potentially affected individuals to watch for suspicious communications.

Finding eight high-severity vulnerabilities in NodeBB in six hours — Should Read

NodeBB versions before 4.14.0 contain eight high-severity vulnerabilities, including XSS, authorization bypasses, private message exposure, post hijacking, and data leaks, many tied to ActivityPub and federation handling. Users should upgrade to 4.14.0 or later to receive the fixes.

  • Aikido found eight high-severity vulnerabilities in NodeBB versions prior to 4.14.0 during a whitebox assessment of the NodeJS-based forum software.
  • The vulnerabilities included multiple cross-site scripting issues, such as unsafe rendering of federated profile icon URLs, unsafe Federation Errors fields in the admin view, and translation template injection after template rendering.
  • Several issues involved authorization or trust failures, including bypassing admin authorization through a custom homepage rewrite, spoofing user IDs to read private messages, and reading private category content through the ActivityPub outbox route.
  • A mass assignment flaw in the topic creation endpoint allowed an attacker to supply a post ID and hijack an existing post, including the default welcome post.
  • NodeBB fixed the reported issues in early July, and the article advises upgrading to version 4.14.0 or newer.

Upbound says hack caused $13 million in fraudulent Acima leases — Should Read

Upbound Group said attackers stole customer data and documents from its systems and used them to create fraudulent Acima lease-to-own agreements, causing about $13 million in losses. The company is adding stronger authentication, fraud detection, and monitoring while law enforcement investigates.

  • Upbound Group disclosed that threat actors stole certain non-sensitive customer information and other documents from its systems without authorization.
  • The stolen information was used to create fraudulent Acima lease-to-own agreements that caused about $13 million in losses in the second quarter of the year.
  • Under the fraudulent agreements, Acima paid participating retailers for goods, but the fraudsters took the merchandise and failed to make the required lease payments.
  • Upbound said it began mitigation and remediation measures with external cybersecurity experts, including enhanced authentication controls, additional fraud-detection mechanisms, and improved monitoring.
  • Federal law enforcement authorities were notified, and no ransomware groups or data extortion threat actors had publicly claimed the attack at publishing time.

Extension of CISA 2015 info-sharing protections passes as part of House’s defense bill — Should Read

The House passed a defense policy bill that includes a 10-year renewal of the 2015 Cybersecurity and Information Sharing Act, restoring legal protections for sharing cyber threat data between industry and government. The extension still faces Senate opposition and must survive negotiations before becoming law.

  • The House passed its version of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, which includes a provision to renew the 2015 Cybersecurity and Information Sharing Act for another decade.
  • CISA 2015 provides legal protections that allow the private sector and federal government to share data on criminal and nation-state hacking threats.
  • The statute briefly expired last year, which the article says left federal officials in the dark about the full scope of digital threats to U.S. critical infrastructure, before it was temporarily extended through September 30.
  • Sen. Rand Paul has vowed to block any reauthorization of CISA 2015 unless language is added barring the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency from work to counter online disinformation.
  • The House-passed NDAA does not include the Senate draft’s provision to merge the Pentagon’s two major cyber roles into a new undersecretary position.

GitHub Cuts Public Bug Bounty Payouts, Moves Top Rewards to VIP Tier — Should Read

GitHub is cutting public bug bounty payouts by at least half from July 27, 2026, while reserving higher rewards and faster access for an invite-only VIP tier. The move reflects growing pressure from AI-assisted vulnerability reports: basic discovery is becoming cheaper and noisier, while verified, high-impact findings remain the most valued.

  • Beginning July 27, 2026, GitHub will cut public bug bounty payouts by at least half at every severity level, with critical findings dropping to a fixed $10,000.
  • GitHub’s invite-only VIP tier will pay higher rewards, including $30,000 or more for critical vulnerabilities, and is intended to give established researchers faster responses and closer access to GitHub’s security engineering team.
  • Reports filed before July 27, 2026, including those already in GitHub’s triage queue, will remain under the previous payout terms.
  • GitHub said the changes are meant to reduce noise and reward higher-quality submissions, while fixed payments are intended to remove uncertainty and triage overhead.
  • The article links GitHub’s changes to a broader shift in which AI can both increase low-quality security reports and help capable researchers and internal teams examine more code more often.

Quarterly Threat Insights – Q2 2026 — Optional

Health-ISAC published the recording and slide deck for its Q2 2026 Quarterly Threat Insights webinar, covering current cyber and physical threats to the health sector, including AI server and MCP exposures, legacy medical IoT risks, geopolitical threat trends, and critical infrastructure policy updates.

  • Health-ISAC’s Quarterly Threat Insights webinar provides a current snapshot of cyber and physical threats facing the health sector.
  • The July 22, 2026 webinar covered the Monthly Cyber Threat Level, mitigating AI Server and MCP exposures in the health sector, and the reality of legacy medical IoT.
  • The webinar also covered geopolitical threat trends in the APAC and LATAM regions, physical security for personnel and facilities, and U.S. critical infrastructure security and resiliency policy updates.
  • Health-ISAC made the webinar recording and PowerPoint slide deck for Quarterly Threat Insights Q2 2026 available online.
  • The next Quarterly Threat Insights session is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM.
